candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because the order service returns 502, which traces show originates from the payment service returning 503 on POST /v1/authorizations. The failure is a downstream server error propagated up the chain (payment -> order -> gateway), not a gateway-local fault.
candidates.uncertainty: Root cause inside payment (config, resource, or dependency) is not observable from gateway-scoped evidence; only the propagated 5xx chain is established.

report.explanation: Traces show a consistent chain: gateway /v1/checkout 502 <- order /v1/orders 502 <- payment /v1/authorizations 503, while inventory/reservations succeed. Gateway logs and metrics confirm 502s on /v1/checkout with low latency, ruling out gateway-local latency. The bounded cause is a downstream server error propagated from payment via order.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/traces for POST /v1/authorizations to determine why it returns 503
Payment service metrics (error rate, saturation, dependency health) during the incident window
